domain_reasoning: The reviewer reads a document and writes comments, so the output is text.
length_reasoning: A short spec or test plan takes twenty minutes to read and comment on; a long design or compliance document takes a few hours.
review_reasoning: A QA lead or author reads the findings and checks the key ones against the document, which takes far less than the original read.
stakes_reasoning: A missed error usually surfaces later in development or testing, but a missed compliance or risk gap can reach release.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's architecture and the team's document standards, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The worker writes an email or letter and logs it on the account, mostly composing text.
length_reasoning: A routine reply takes a few minutes; a claim result with explanation and adjustments takes half an hour.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the message and the account notes against the case facts.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong answer reaches the customer and causes a complaint or rework, and a wrong claim outcome can carry financial or regulatory exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's policies, claim rules and templates, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into pricing the service and taking payment in billing systems.
length_reasoning: A simple quote and payment takes a few minutes; a deposit or billing set-up with several options takes up to fifteen.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the contact and checks the amount and receipt in the billing record.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong charge is usually caught at reconciliation or by the customer, but larger amounts mean financial loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's price lists and billing rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into pulling data from test management tools and working in spreadsheets or dashboards.
length_reasoning: A quick look at one suite takes an hour; a multi-release trend study takes a day.
review_reasoning: The manager checks the data pulls, the trend claims and whether the recommendations follow, which takes a fraction of the analysis time.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong trend claim leads to misdirected test effort, caught later, but a large one can steer release decisions.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the team's test suites, flaky tests and release history, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The worker gathers examples and writes up a recommendation document.
length_reasoning: A short note on a clear recurring issue takes an hour; one needing data and several examples takes a day.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the write-up and spot-checks a few cited examples.
stakes_reasoning: A weak recommendation is usually ignored or sent back, with little harm.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the company's processes and customer history, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into entering complaint details in the case or CRM system.
length_reasoning: A simple complaint takes a few minutes; a detailed one with account lookups takes fifteen.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the contact and compares it with the recorded details.
stakes_reasoning: Missing or wrong details cause rework by the investigators and annoy the customer, but can be fixed by calling back.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's complaint categories and tools, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is writing and testing code for the tool.
length_reasoning: A small helper or script takes half a day; a framework component with design, review and rollout takes days to weeks, so there are two groups.
review_reasoning: A code reviewer reads the change, runs it and checks tests and design.
stakes_reasoning: A flaw shows as flaky or wrong test results that mislead the team and take rework, but is reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's codebase, test infrastructure and conventions, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The work is in monitoring tools, system consoles and ticketing.
length_reasoning: Most alerts are transient and closed in minutes; a real fault can take over an hour to trace.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the cause note and checks it against the alert data.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly closed alert usually recurs, but a missed fault can become an outage.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the organisation's systems and their normal behaviour, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into configuring templates, macros and settings in the application.
length_reasoning: A template tweak takes half an hour; a script or macro with testing and release takes a day, so there are two groups.
review_reasoning: The reviewer reads the change, tries it and checks it against the request.
stakes_reasoning: A bad change affects users and needs rework or rollback, but is reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's applications, processes and user needs, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The worker observes the software in use and writes up findings.
length_reasoning: A brief remote check takes a couple of hours; an on-site visit with testing and a report takes a day or two.
review_reasoning: The test lead reads the report and checks key claims against logs or notes.
stakes_reasoning: Missed problems reach the release and cause customer complaints, but can be patched.
context_reasoning: Needs the product and the beta customer's setup, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is running installers and setting options in the tool and its environment.
length_reasoning: A simple upgrade takes twenty minutes; a new install with integrations and licensing takes a few hours.
review_reasoning: A colleague checks that the tool runs and the team can use it.
stakes_reasoning: Problems show up quickly as the tool fails for users and are fixed.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's environment and integrations, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into scripting and configuring servers, services and data.
length_reasoning: A small environment takes half a day; a complex multi-tier replica takes days.
review_reasoning: Testers compare the configuration with the production spec and run checks, which takes an hour or so.
stakes_reasoning: A mismatch gives misleading performance results that cost rework, but the environment can be rebuilt.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of the production architecture and the company's infrastructure, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The worker reads documentation, tries tools and writes a recommendation.
length_reasoning: A quick comparison of two tools takes half a day; a full trial of several takes days.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the report and checks the criteria and key findings.
stakes_reasoning: A poor recommendation causes wasted cost and a later migration, which is costly but slow-burning.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's workflow and existing tools, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into reading applications, interviewing and writing a recommendation.
length_reasoning: A small pool takes half a day; a large pool with several interviews takes more than a day.
review_reasoning: HR checks the recommendation and the notes behind it.
stakes_reasoning: A bad hire is costly but reversible within the probation period.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's needs and the company's hiring process, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking up the account and usage data.
length_reasoning: A simple lookup takes a few minutes; a case needing history and weather or usage analysis takes up to eighteen.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer listens to the call and checks the account data behind the explanation.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong assessment leads to an escalation or complaint, or to an unjustified refusal, but can be reversed.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's billing systems and policies, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is operating installers, settings and the ticket system on a user's machine.
length_reasoning: A standard install takes about ten minutes; a repair needing troubleshooting takes over an hour.
review_reasoning: The support lead checks the ticket and the software works.
stakes_reasoning: A bad install is found by the user quickly and redone.
context_reasoning: A skilled outsider following the specification could do it nearly as fast.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into monitoring dashboards, logs and profiling tools.
length_reasoning: A threshold breach that is noise takes minutes; a real regression takes hours to trace.
review_reasoning: A lead reads the findings and checks them against metrics or logs.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly closed issue recurs in production, and a missed one can cause an outage.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of the system's normal behaviour and history, built over months.
